An unfounded block forwarded verbatim is still an unfounded block. Fixed by destructuring the four ETJ fields OUT before spreading, and pinned by two new tests (a stale conflict must not survive the city-limits reading changing to unincorporated; a stale reason must not survive a determination arriving). Found by test, not by review - which is the point of pre-registering.

Distinct parcels counted (`count(distinct county_fips||':'||prop_id)`), so a parcel inside two rings of one city is one parcel. Same-city is the right join because the conflict the panel declares is between TWO READS OF ONE PLACE: the city-limits read names a city and the ETJ read names a ring; both name the same city in the live conflict case (Austin / austin-tx:39). cooccurrence.query: P:/seat-worktrees/p332-etj-panel/_p332_cooccurrence_final.sql (the second, validated run) and _p332_cooccurrence.sql (the first). Both are left in place in the seat worktree, outside the product repo. The decisive part of the validated query: a MATERIALIZED `p` CTE of deduped in-city points, a MATERIALIZED `citypoly` CTE of ST_MakeValid city polygons, and a MATERIALIZED `strip` CTE where each ring's geometry is ST_MakeValid'd and, only where the ring actually intersects its own city polygon, reduced by ST_Difference(ring, city). Two counts per city: ST_Contains(ring, pt) and ST_Contains(strip, pt).
cooccurrence.theJoinKeyCorrection: The first validated run joined each ETJ ring to in-city parcels on a normalization of the ring's `city_key` (`lower(regexp_replace(regexp_replace(city_key,'-tx$',''),'[^a-zA-Z0-9]','','g'))`) equalling the same normalization of the jurisdiction row's `city_name`. That silently DROPPED Bastrop: the store's key is `bastrop-city-tx`, which normalizes to `bastropcity`, while the jurisdiction rows name the city `Bastrop` (`bastrop`), so no equality holds and Bastrop's parcels fell outside a total that presented itself as covering all six counties. Re-joining on the ring's OWN `city_name` column (tx_etj_boundary carries the publisher's city name, `Bastrop`) matched it and added 269 full-ring / 69 strip-only parcels, both rings: bastrop-city-tx:3 262 full / 69 strip, bastrop-city-tx:4 7 full / 0 strip. Audited every other key for the same failure (_p332_bastrop.sql C1, all 20 keys): `bastrop-city-tx` is the ONLY key whose name and key normalize differently, and the six keys that match nothing under EITHER spelling (belton, cibolo, killeen, new-braunfels, san-antonio, seguin) are 0 because those cities have no in-city parcels inside the six Phase 0 counties at all - they are outside-county rings, 0 in the per-ring scan too, so they are not omissions. headline.coverageTravelsWithItsDenominator: 77,459 / 611,116 = 12.67% of the six counties' in-city parcels would be served `conflicting` by the panel's rule. The strip-only population is 2,160 / 611,116 = 0.354%.
headline.theSplitIsTheFinding: 75,299 of the 77,459 (97.2%) are parcels where the ring POLYGON OVERLAPS THE CITY'S OWN LIMITS, which is a ring-drawing convention and not a disagreement about the parcel. 74,785 of those (96.5% of the whole total) come from just three single-polygon publishers - Georgetown 38,890, Leander 31,644, Dripping Springs 3,842. 2,160 (2.8% of the total, 0.35% of in-city) are inside a ring that genuinely lies OUTSIDE the city's limits, which is the population where two independently derived reads actually disagree; Austin contributes 541 of them, Kyle 175, Dripping Springs 173.

mechanismMeasurement.theDispatchRequiredASecondMechanism: 'Measure; do not pick.' CP1 stated M1-M5 as candidates. The store read SETTLES the dominant mechanism, and it is M2, not M1.
mechanismMeasurement.decisiveTest: For each city, does its published ETJ ring contain the city's OWN representative point, ST_PointOnSurface(tx_city_boundary.geometry)? `true` for exactly three rings: dripping-springs-tx:1, georgetown-tx:9644, leander-tx:1. `false` for every ring of every other city - including all 298 Austin rings, all 23 Taylor rings and all 14 Kyle rings.
mechanismMeasurement.independentConfirmation: Those same three cities' full-ring counts equal ~100% of their own in-city denominator - Georgetown 39,015 of 39,015 in-city parcels (100.00%), Leander 31,755 of 31,779 (99.92%), Dripping Springs 4,015 of 4,016 (99.98%). A genuine ETJ strip cannot produce that: an extraterritorial jurisdiction is by definition OUTSIDE the city's limits, so a count that swallows the whole city is a property of the polygon, not of the parcels.
mechanismMeasurement.soWhatM1IsStillTrueFor: The remaining 2,160 strip-only parcels are the population consistent with CP1's leading candidate M1 (landing_parcel_jurisdiction reporting the jurisdiction that GOVERNS the point - which can be a city whose ETJ the point sits in - rather than literal in-city status). The live probe parcel 48453:134392 is one of them: per the P-204 artifact its situs is 'unincorporated, inside Austin's 2-mile ETJ' while the jurisdiction row reads in-city Austin.
mechanismMeasurement.andWhatThisDoesNotDecide: Whether the jurisdiction row or the ring is the wrong one for those 2,160 parcels is a store-ownership question, not a panel question, and this lane does not decide it. WHICH SIDE IS WRONG DOES NOT CHANGE WHAT THE PANEL SHOULD SERVE: in both populations the two reads genuinely disagree as served, so `conflicting` is correct in both - the difference is who owes the fix.
